name: Grande Ronde River (Troy – Heller Bar)
gaugeName: Grande Ronde River at Troy, OR
blurb: Multi-day canyon trip from Troy to the Snake River at Heller Bar.

sections.notes: Usually 2–3 days. The Narrows (Class IV-, AW mile ~21.5 below Boggan's) is the crux — scout. Ends with a short float on the Snake to Heller Bar. Miles: 19.5 Troy–Boggan's plus 26.7 Boggan's–Snake (AW). Oregon Waterway Access Permit on the Oregon portion (all non-motorized boats as of 2026). Heller Bar is a WDFW water access area — Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass for parking.

putInAccess.operator: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
putInAccess.sourceName: Oregon State Marine Board Boating Access Sites (public), 'Troy Access' (ObjectId 287; manager/owner ODFW; facility Boat Ramp; public_display Yes)
putInAccess.note: Batch 2. Troy is in Oregon (Wallowa County). Coordinate is the Oregon State Marine Board's own boating-access point, which lists ODFW as manager and owner, 1 trailered ramp lane and parking. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/troy.png) puts it at the head of the gravel access on the south-east bank just upstream (south-west) of the Troy bridge, about 10-15 m from the water through the tree gap; the v1/OSM point is ~40 m away. Legal access: OSMB lists it as a public boating access site (OSMB boat-ramp map), and BLM's Wallowa & Grande Ronde Wild and Scenic Rivers page names Troy as a river access point. The OSMB record has fees='Yes' but USEFEE='No'; fee status is unclear. BLM says free self-issued river permits are required for boating the Wallowa/Grande Ronde in Oregon.
putInAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~47 on the flowline), the access is on the south-east bank, right of the NHD centreline. Confirmed on imagery.

takeOutAccess.operator: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
takeOutAccess.sourceName: WDFW Facilities GIS, Boat Ramp layer (feature 244, concrete)
takeOutAccess.note: Batch 2. Coordinate is WDFW's own boat-ramp feature. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/heller.png) puts it on the concrete ramp about 7 m from the water on the Snake River's west bank below the Grande Ronde confluence, matching the v1 instruction to pull out river-left after entering the Snake. WDFW's hand-launch feature (layer 4, 53) is ~300 m south and was not used. Legal access: WDFW Heller Bar page (https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/water-access-sites/heller-bar-395) lists it in the Chief Joseph Wildlife Area Unit, open year-round, 1 concrete ramp and 1 hand launch, camping allowed; WaterAccessSites layer (https://geodataservices.wdfw.wa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/WP_RealEstate/WaterAccessSites/FeatureServer/1) shows WDFW-managed, no closure. Pass required.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream on the Snake (flow bearing ~5, north), the ramp is on the west bank, left of the NHD centreline. Confirmed on imagery.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 2). Both endpoints are verified. Troy comes from OSMB (ODFW-managed) and Heller Bar from WDFW ramp feature 244 (Chief Joseph Wildlife Area Unit). Banks come from NHDPlus HR. The Heller Bar take-out is on the Snake's west bank (river-left) just below the confluence.
